soundness_flags.label: ass:positive-population-margins
soundness_flags.one_line: Positive selected-table cells and c=P(S=1)>0 already imply P(E=e)>0 for every e in every compatible SCM, so this is not an independent load-bearing assumption.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 6 (separated Wald)
soundness_flags.one_line: F_chi is defined only on rigid charts, but the selector's empty-set fallback can choose an arbitrary chart, leaving the globally defined estimator and Wald region undefined on that event.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 2 (Tian–Pearl reduction)
soundness_flags.one_line: Its no-selection, exogeneity, and monotonicity special-case hypotheses are neither assumptions nor explicit theorem dependencies; state S=1 a.s. (or equivalent), X⊥U, and P(U=3)=0.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 6 (separated Wald)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Regular Wald inference is restricted to separated rigid charts with common first-order map, C2 extensions, and covariance bounded away from singularity.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The Wald limit and coverage claim is conditional on membership in the separated rigid stratum, not a transition-law result.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 7 (confidence-fiber coverage)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Transition laws receive finite-sample coverage only; first-order Wald agreement is restricted to separated rigid strata.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Coverage holds throughout the fiber, while root-n Hausdorff agreement and shrinking local geometry are asserted only on the stated regular stratum.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 2 (GEUVADIS audit)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The application conditions on proxy exclusion, outcome-dependent selection, and IV assumptions.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The audit certifies consequences within the proposed SCM rather than empirically validating its graph.
